prompt: Egocentric nadir capture from a DJI Matrice survey drone at 80 metres AGL over a suburban residential block, the downward-facing mapping camera looking straight at the ground. A single blue residential swimming pool is the salient object at the frame centre, its rectangular shape and the surrounding concrete deck sharp against the mown lawn. Adjacent rooftops with asphalt shingles and rain gutters tile the frame in a grid, and backyard fences, trampolines, and garden sheds are visible at their actual plan-view shapes. The image is high-resolution but flat—no shadows to speak of in the overcast midday light, and the colour is slightly desaturated from the haze layer between the drone and the ground. A faint circular vignette darkens the frame corners from the lens, and the GPS overlay reads LAT 33.7490 LON -84.3880 ALT 82m in small green text at the bottom-left. A lawnmower has left visible stripe patterns in one yard.

Egocentric forward-facing camera capture from a delivery drone at 15 metres AGL flying along a suburban cul-de-sac. A single red USPS mailbox on a post at the curb is directly ahead and below the flight path, its pull-down door and collection-time placard in sharp focus. The street's asphalt, sidewalk seams, and parked minivans stretch outward in the wide-angle perspective, and the drone's own landing gear legs intrude as two dark bars at the bottom corners of the frame. The image has the slight rolling-shutter wobble of a lightweight gimbal compensating for wind gusts—the mailbox is sharp but the tree canopy at the frame edge shows horizontal jello distortion. A motion shadow of the drone itself is faintly visible on the driveway pavement below, and the camera's auto-exposure has slightly crushed the shadows under the parked cars.

Egocentric nadir capture from an inspection drone hovering at 30 metres above an industrial warehouse rooftop. A single large HVAC unit with a rusted housing and spinning fan blades is at the frame centre, the blades motion-blurred into a disc. The flat roof membrane's gravel ballast and the seams between roofing sections radiate outward, and standing water from a recent rain pools in the membrane's sags, reflecting the grey sky. The drone's shadow is a small dark cross on the gravel directly below, and a maintenance access hatch and a pipe vent stack are visible nearby. The image is sharp at the centre but softens at the edges from the lens's field curvature, and the overall tone is flat grey-on-grey with low contrast. A bird dropping on the camera's lens glass creates a small translucent smear at the upper-right.

Egocentric forward-tilted camera capture from an inspection drone flying under a concrete highway overpass at 5 metres AGL, looking up at the bridge's underside. A single corroded expansion joint with exposed rebar and spalling concrete is at the frame centre, the rust stains and delamination cracks in high-resolution detail. The bridge's parallel girders and the formwork marks on the concrete deck stretch outward, and the daylight at the bridge's edges is blown out to white. The drone's propeller tips are visible as faint motion-blurred arcs at the top corners of the frame, and the downwash creates a visible disturbance in a puddle on the road surface below. The image is underexposed on the shadowed concrete to preserve the highlight detail at the bridge edges, and the auto-white-balance has shifted warm from the orange rust reflected on the grey surfaces. A pigeon nest is wedged in a girder flange to the left.

Egocentric nadir capture from an agricultural survey drone at 40 metres AGL over a centre-pivot irrigated cornfield. A single failed irrigation sprinkler head—visible as a brown dry patch in an otherwise green field—is the salient anomaly at the frame centre. The corn rows create a fine linear texture radiating outward from the pivot point, and the circular irrigation track's wheel ruts are visible as parallel arcs in the soil. The image is captured with a modified multispectral camera—the colour rendition is slightly false, with the healthy corn appearing an over-vivid emerald and the stressed patch a desaturated yellow-brown. The lens is clean but the altitude introduces atmospheric haze that reduces contrast at the frame edges, and the shadow of the drone is a tiny dark speck on the crop canopy. A dirt access road and a grain silo are at the field's boundary at the frame's far edge.

Egocentric forward-facing camera capture from a street-mapping drone at 25 metres AGL flying along a main commercial street in a mid-size American city. A single city bus stopped at a bus shelter is the salient object, its roof-mounted HVAC unit and route-number display visible from above at an oblique angle. The street's lane markings, parking meters, and tree canopies are sharp below, and the storefronts' awnings and sidewalk café tables are visible in plan. The drone's two front propeller guards enter the frame as dark semicircles at the top corners, and the image has the flat, GIS-data quality of a systematic mapping pass—no artistic composition, the bus is slightly off-centre as the drone follows its programmed flight line. The building shadows are short, indicating near-noon sun, and the shadow of a pedestrian on the sidewalk is more visible than the pedestrian themselves. A slight cyan fringing is visible on high-contrast roof edges.

Egocentric oblique capture from a utility-inspection drone at 20 metres AGL, camera tilted 45 degrees toward a wooden power pole. A single ceramic insulator with a visible hairline crack is the salient object, the crack's dark line running through the brown glaze. The pole's creosote-treated wood grain and the bolted crossarm are in high-resolution detail, and the power lines extend outward in both directions, sagging between poles. The drone's camera gimbal vibrates faintly from a rotor harmonic, creating a micro-blur that is visible on the wires as a doubled edge but not on the stationary insulator. The background is a residential neighbourhood of rooftops and driveways, defocused by the shallow depth created by the close inspection distance. A woodpecker hole in the pole is visible just below the crossarm.

Egocentric nadir capture from a survey drone at 50 metres AGL over a big-box retail parking lot at mid-morning. A single white box truck is parked diagonally across two spaces near the loading dock, its roof and the company logo painted on top visible from directly above. The parking lot's grid of white-striped spaces, cart corrals, and lamp post bases tile the asphalt in a regular pattern, and the painted arrows and COMPACT ONLY text are legible. The image is sharp and high-resolution but entirely flat—nadir removes all sense of depth, and the vehicles are recognisable only by their roof shapes and shadows. The drone's shadow is a small dark plus sign on the asphalt two rows from the truck. A heat island shimmer from the dark asphalt creates a faint waviness at the frame edges, and the overall colour is the grey-and-white monotony of a parking lot from above, interrupted only by the coloured car roofs.

Egocentric forward-facing camera capture from a railway-inspection drone at 12 metres AGL, flying along the centreline of a single-track rail corridor. A single broken rail joint with a visible gap in the steel is the salient defect, the gap catching the light as a bright line across the rust-brown rail head. The wooden sleepers and the ballast gravel create a repeating texture receding into the distance, and the rail's gauge and the fishplate bolts are in sharp detail. The drone's propeller wash disturbs loose ballast dust into a faint haze below, and the camera's vibration isolation is imperfect—a micro-jitter doubles the rail edges in alternating frames. Weeds growing between the sleepers and a discarded plastic bag snagged on the fence wire are visible at the edges. The image is flat rural landscape on both sides—ploughed fields and a distant grain elevator under a washed-out white sky.

Egocentric nadir capture from an emergency-response drone at 60 metres AGL over a flood zone, looking straight down at a residential neighbourhood with standing brown water in every street and yard. A single house with a bright blue tarp on its damaged roof is the salient object at the centre, the tarp's colour vivid against the brown water and the grey-green canopy of partially submerged trees. Debris—a mattress, a plastic cooler, branches—floats in the floodwater around the house's foundation. The image is high-resolution but the colour is flat and muddy, the brown water reducing the scene to a monochrome of earth tones broken only by the tarp and a few car rooftops barely above the waterline. The drone's battery indicator—78%—is overlaid in the upper-right, and the GPS coordinates are stamped at the bottom. A rescue boat's wake is a faint V-shape in the water two blocks away.

Egocentric side-facing camera capture from an inspection drone orbiting a cell tower at 3 metres distance. A single corroded coaxial cable connector on the antenna mounting bracket is the salient defect, the green oxidation on the brass fitting visible in macro-like detail. The tower's galvanised steel lattice structure fills the frame with repeating triangular geometry, and the antenna panels, cable runs, and obstruction-light housing are in sharp focus. The drone's prop guard is a dark arc at the frame's left edge, and the downwash ruffles a loose cable tie on the bracket. The background is a distant landscape of fields and a highway interchange, severely defocused by the close working distance. The image has a slight blue-grey cast from the overcast sky reflecting off the steel, and the camera's auto-focus has hunted slightly—the near cable is perfectly sharp but the lattice members 30 centimetres behind show a soft halo.

Egocentric nadir capture from an inspection drone at 25 metres AGL over a utility-scale solar farm. A single cracked photovoltaic panel is the salient defect, the fracture line visible as a dark diagonal across the panel's blue-black surface. The solar array's regular grid of identical panels fills the frame in a tiled pattern, each panel's aluminium frame and the gravel-covered ground between the rows creating a precise geometric texture. The cracked panel is slightly discoloured—a brownish hotspot where the cell has degraded. The image is captured in the infrared-adjacent spectrum, giving the panels an unnaturally dark blue appearance and the gravel a warm tan. The drone's shadow crosses two panels at the frame's lower edge, and the straight rows of the array warp slightly at the fisheye periphery. A maintenance vehicle's white roof is visible at the array's access road at the far edge.

Egocentric forward-facing camera capture from a construction-monitoring drone at 35 metres AGL, flying over an active building site. A single tower crane is the salient object, its yellow lattice boom extending across the frame at a slight angle, the hook block and a suspended concrete bucket visible mid-pour. The building's reinforced-concrete frame is partially complete—three floors of columns and slabs with rebar poking from the top. The site's red clay earth, equipment staging area, and construction trailers are visible below, and workers in hard hats are tiny bright dots on the deck. The image has the systematic, documentation quality of a weekly progress capture—datestamp visible, composition centred on the crane, no creative framing. Wind vibration creates a slight directional blur on the crane's cable, and the camera lens has a speck of dried mud at the seven-o'clock position creating a tiny soft spot.

Egocentric nadir capture from a traffic-monitoring drone at 100 metres AGL over a highway interchange cloverleaf. A single overturned semi-truck on the exit ramp is the salient incident, its white trailer lying on its side, cargo scattered across the ramp and shoulder. Emergency vehicles—a fire engine and two police cars with roof lights visible as tiny coloured dots—surround the scene, and orange cones close the ramp. The interchange's looping ramps and the mainline traffic are visible from directly above, vehicles reduced to their roof-plan silhouettes. The image is high-altitude and slightly hazy, the atmospheric scatter reducing contrast on the far sections of highway. The drone's nadir perspective removes all depth, and the cloverleaf's geometry is a textbook overhead diagram. The timestamp reads 2024-03-15 08:22:41 and the altitude overlay shows 102m AGL.

Egocentric oblique capture from a survey drone at 20 metres AGL flying along a coastal bluff, camera tilted 30 degrees toward the cliff face. A single fresh landslide scar exposing raw brown earth and severed tree roots is the salient feature, the scarp's vertical face in sharp detail against the surrounding green grass. The beach below is littered with slide debris—soil clumps, fence posts, a section of sidewalk—and the surf is a white fringe at the sand's edge. The drone's shadow races along the beach below at the frame's bottom. The image has the workmanlike quality of a geotechnical survey capture—the flight path follows the bluff edge systematically, and the composition is functional, not aesthetic. Salt spray from the surf has deposited a fine residue on the camera glass, reducing contrast slightly, and the wind at the cliff edge causes a visible gimbal correction—one frame edge is a pixel lower than the other.

Egocentric forward-facing camera capture from a fire-monitoring drone at 60 metres AGL flying over a forest fire's active edge. A single spot fire ahead of the main front is the salient element—a tree crown fully engulfed in orange flame, isolated from the main burn line by 50 metres of unburned green canopy. Thick grey-white smoke drifts across the upper half of the frame, obscuring the sky entirely, and the main fire front is a ragged orange line in the mid-ground. The image is severely colour-shifted—the smoke gives everything a yellow-orange cast, and the camera's auto-exposure oscillates between the bright flames and the dark unburned forest, producing a noisy, poorly exposed compromise. Ash particles on the camera lens create dozens of tiny out-of-focus grey spots, and the heat shimmer from the fire distorts the treeline in a visible ripple. The drone's telemetry overlay shows wind speed 15 kt, heading 270, and battery 42%.

Egocentric nadir capture from an archaeology survey drone at 15 metres AGL over a ploughed field in the English midlands. A single circular crop mark—the ghostly outline of a buried Bronze Age ring ditch visible as a darker green circle in the young wheat—is the salient feature at the frame centre. The plough furrows create a fine linear texture across the field, and the crop mark's diameter is roughly 20 metres, the ditch's path showing as a subtle tonal difference in the crop vigour. The image requires close inspection to see the feature—it is not dramatic, just a faint ring in an otherwise uniform green field. The surrounding hedgerow boundaries and a farm track are at the frame edges. The camera is a modified NIR sensor for vegetation analysis, giving the wheat an unnaturally bright false-green and the bare soil a pink tone. The drone's shadow is a sharp dark cross on the wheat directly below.

Egocentric forward-facing camera capture from a search-and-rescue drone at 30 metres AGL flying a grid pattern over dense temperate forest. A single orange emergency bivvy shelter visible through a gap in the canopy is the salient object, the bright nylon fabric a vivid spot of colour against the dark green of Douglas fir crowns. The canopy gaps and the tree crowns' texture fill the frame, and the forest floor is only intermittently visible as dark patches between the branches. The image is captured in late afternoon, and the low sun angle creates long tree shadows that stripe the canopy in a confusing pattern of light and dark. The drone's thermal-camera overlay is not shown, but the visible-light image alone makes the orange shelter detectable primarily by colour contrast. A stream's glint is visible through the trees at the frame's right edge, and the camera has auto-focused on the canopy layer, leaving the shelter slightly soft.

Egocentric nadir capture from a roof-inspection drone hovering at 8 metres above a residential asphalt-shingle roof. A single patch of missing shingles exposing the tar-paper underlayment is the salient damage at the frame centre, the dark exposed rectangle contrasting with the grey shingles. The roof's ridge line, hip joints, and plumbing vent boots are in detail, and the gutter is visible at the roof edge with a clump of leaves blocking the downspout. The close hover distance means the image fills the frame with only the roof surface—no ground or horizon visible, just shingles, flashing, and a satellite dish. The drone's rotor wash lifts a loose shingle tab at the damage edge, caught mid-flutter. The image is sharp and well-exposed from the overcast light, but the flat nadir angle makes the roof's slope invisible—it reads as a flat plane. Lichen growth on the north-facing shingles appears as pale green patches.

Egocentric oblique capture from an inspection drone hovering 5 metres from a wind turbine blade at hub height, roughly 80 metres above ground. A single lightning-strike damage site on the blade's leading edge is the salient defect—a blackened pit in the fibreglass composite with radiating cracks. The blade's white surface fills most of the frame, its curvature and the internal spar's faint outline visible through the translucent composite skin. The nacelle and hub are in the background, slightly defocused, and the other two blades extend out of frame. The ground far below is a patchwork of green fields reduced to a blurred texture by the extreme altitude and the lens's shallow depth of field at close working distance. The drone's propeller wash creates no visible effect on the massive blade, but the camera gimbal's vibration dampening is imperfect—the blade surface shows a faint directional micro-blur. Wind noise is implied by the gimbal's slight off-axis tilt visible in the horizon line.
